narrative: (Policyholder with Suncorp home and contents insurance, including accidental damage cover.) On 2 August 2026 the hot water tank in our garage burst at the base overnight. The water ran out under the garage door onto the driveway so nothing else was damaged, but the tank itself is finished. A plumber quoted $2,400 to remove it and install a replacement tank. Policy number SUN-5520913.
tests: SPDS: Suncorp Contents SPDS (June 2026) replaces the PDS p.75 accidental-damage exclusion; repairing/replacing items that burst or leak (e.g. hot water tank) is not covered

narrative: (Policyholder with GIO home and contents insurance, including accidental damage cover.) On 19 July 2026 the boiler in our benchtop espresso machine exploded while it was heating up. Nobody was hurt and the kitchen is fine apart from a bit of water on the bench, but the machine is a write-off. It cost $1,800 and I'd like it replaced.
tests: SPDS: GIO Contents SPDS (July 2026) widens the PDS p.77 exclusion from 'tanks or containers that burst or leak' to 'items that explode, burst, or leak'; the old wording arguably wouldn't have excluded an exploding appliance

narrative: (Policyholder with BudgetDirect home and contents insurance. I didn't take the accidental damage option.) On 6 January 2026 a bushfire burned through bushland about 2 kilometres from our house. The fire never reached our street, but smoke and ash came in through the vents for two days and the curtains, couch and ceilings are stained and smell. Cleaning and replacing the curtains is quoted at $3,100.
tests: SPDS: Budget Direct SPDS Part 2 replaces the PDS p.31 Fire event; heat/ash/smoke/soot from a fire over 100 metres away is not covered unless the Accidental Damage option was chosen

narrative: (Policyholder with ING contents insurance. I own an apartment in a strata building.) On 11 September 2026 a storm knocked out power in our building and when it came back the electric hot water system inside my apartment had failed and the air conditioning unit wouldn't start. An electrician says both need replacing, around $4,200 in total. I haven't checked with the body corporate yet.
tests: SPDS: ING SPDS (March 2026) adds cover for strata unit owners' hot water systems and air conditioners under contents, but excludes items the body corporate's policy covers or should cover

narrative: (Policyholder with CGU home insurance.) On 22 June 2026 strong winds during a storm blew over about 15 metres of our timber side fence. A fencing contractor quoted $3,200 to replace it. Policy number CGU-HB-771204.
tests: PDS: CGU storm cover for fences (CGU SPDS only changes the insurer entity, so it shouldn't affect the decision)

narrative: (Policyholder with CommBank home insurance.) On 14 March 2026 a hailstorm cracked a lot of the roof tiles on our house and rain got into the ceiling of the main bedroom. A roofer quoted $4,800 for the tiles and the ceiling repair.
tests: New insurer. Storm cover is on CommBank Home PDS p.23; a known retrieval gap puts that page outside the top 15 for 'storm damage to my roof'

narrative: (Policyholder with Westpac home and contents insurance.) On 3 May 2026 someone broke in through the back sliding door while we were at work and took a laptop and some jewellery. Police attended and gave us an event number. The laptop was $1,900 and the jewellery about $1,600.
tests: New insurer. Theft/burglary under contents; possible jewellery sub-limit

narrative: (Policyholder with Shannons home contents insurance.) On 28 August 2026 my son knocked our 65-inch TV off the entertainment unit while playing and the screen cracked. It cost $1,600 two years ago. I'm not sure whether our policy includes accidental damage.
tests: New insurer. Accidental damage to a TV may depend on an optional cover the claimant can't confirm

narrative: (Policyholder with RACWA building and contents insurance.) We took out our policy on 1 February 2026 because we'd never had home insurance before. The next day, 2 February 2026, heavy rain caused the river to flood and water came through the ground floor. Carpets, a lounge suite and the lower plasterboard are damaged, estimated at $14,000.
tests: New insurer. RAC WA Home PDS p.10 excludes flood in the first 48 hours after the policy starts, unless it began on taking possession of the building or replaced an expired policy with no gap

narrative: (Policyholder with RACWA landlord insurance.) Our tenant moved out on 30 June 2026 and left holes punched in several walls and a broken internal door. The property manager thinks it was done deliberately. The repair quote is $2,700. Policy number RAC-LL-30918.
tests: New insurer, Landlord product. Malicious damage by a tenant under landlord cover
